summary: ```markdown # Clo Ai Studio | Clo 2025.1 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, it's Phoebe, and I'm going to talk all about our AI features, how to access them, how to use them, and everything AI. So let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Accessing AI Features So, I have my screen in front of me here, and this is something you'll see if you don't have anything activated or on. You’ll probably notice some grayed-out sections, like our old AI logo and everything there. If you click on it or hover over it, you'll get some information indicating that the AI plugin is not activated. To activate it, you need to go to your CloAdmin. This applies to any of the AI features. For example, if I select my fabric here, you’ll see that the magic wand is deactivated. Again, hovering over it will provide some guidance. ## Activating AI Features in Enterprise and Individual Accounts If I go into my render window, you’ll see that it’s even grayed out there. You might be asking, "How do I get there?" Let’s start with enterprise users. If you are an admin and have already associated with Clo, you need to open Clo and go to your page. If you are not an admin, you’ll need to ask your admin to give you access. For admins, log in to your account, and navigate to the AI Studio plugin. Everything will appear inactive. To change that, click on the edit button, select what you want on or off, and then hit save. You might see a pop-up asking you to confirm that you're okay with using this stuff externally. Once that’s set, hit okay. For individual users, the process is similar. You’ll see the grayed-out AI features, and you can hover over them to access CloAdmin. Then, go to your personal page, navigate to the AI Studio plugin, and hit edit. After confirming any pop-ups, select the features you want to activate. Don’t forget to hit save and then reopen Clo to access the activated AI features. ## Overview of AI Studio Features Now, let’s explore the different AI features we have. We are currently in the AI Studio, which is in beta. Here, you’ll see all of your options and features, as well as what’s new in embroidery. ### AI Graphics Generator Let’s start with the AI graphics generator. To use it, you can select either image or text. I’ll stick with text and type in "lion face" with a pop art style. Once I hit generate, I can view the results. If I want another version, I can hit generate again, or use a random prompt for variety. Once I find a design I like, I can apply it to my project. The history of all the graphics I've generated can be accessed through the clock icon. ### Embroidery Feature In addition to graphics, you can upload images for embroidery. For example, I can upload a pineapple image and select options to transform it into an embroidery design. After previewing and applying it, I can continue exploring different variations and styles. ### Texture Selection Next, let's move to texture. I can select different AI options, choose a fabric, and generate prints. For instance, if I choose a tartan check pattern with a specific print size, I can generate the fabric pattern and pin it for rendering later. ### Understanding Pattern Size It’s important to understand what pattern size means in this context. The pattern size indicates the size of the design, not the fabric itself. For example, a pattern size of one corresponds to approximately 1024 pixels, whereas a size of four increases that to around 4096 pixels. ## Pattern Drafter Now, let’s jump into the pattern drafter. The AI can create a shirt based on measurements, but it can also work from any uploaded image. This is great for incorporating sketches or photos taken in stores. You can edit the generated pattern, adjusting it as needed with simple or general options based on your familiarity with pattern editing. ## Rendering Features Let’s move to the rendering feature. Here, you can upload a target image or use random prompts to create visuals. You can refine elements like hair, hands, and garments, adjusting them as necessary. Once satisfied, you can save your render, and there are also options for background customization. You can generate various backgrounds and adjust their properties to fit your designs. ## Conclusion In conclusion, this is how all the AI features work within Clo. You can always refer back to your history to see both your graphics and renders. Remember, you can save any creations you want to use later. Thank you so much for watching! If you have any questions, feel free to use the comment section below. Don’t forget to like and subscribe for more great content about Clo. Keep having fun in Clo! ```
